title: Simulated Launch Playground and Canary SLA Timing Matrix
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: Recent release trains experienced unpredictable post-cut latency spikes when traffic shape varied across regions. We need a repeatable dry-run surface that lets PM/Eng/Infra rehearse a release under synthetic and sampled production traffic to validate canary timing, autoscale policies, and rollback thresholds.

Goal: Build a simulated launch playground and formalize a Canary SLA Timing Matrix that maps observable thresholds (p95 latency, error rate, GPU utilization, queue depth) to automated and manual rollback/mitigation actions. Deliverables: (1) Simulation harness in staging that replays traffic patterns and can run 'what-if' autoscale scenarios, (2) Canary SLA Timing Matrix doc used by on-call and launch owners, (3) Owner roster and backstop protocol for first-2-hours post-cut, and (4) a runbook template for pre-flight rehearsal and post-cut assessment.
acceptance_criteria: Playground can replay three canonical traffic profiles (steady, bursty ramp, regional shift) against staging runtime with configurable user counts and seq lengths
Canary SLA Timing Matrix produced and ratified by ENG, SRE, and PM — mapping thresholds to actions (auto-scale, pause traffic, rollback)
Two cross-team rehearsals executed with stakeholders, documented findings and action items
Post-cut backstop roster published in Console on-call panel and included in launch runbook
decisions: Use sampled production traces (1% reservoir) + synthetic amplification for burst scenarios to avoid sensitive data export
Default canary window set to 15m for latency-sensitive paths and 30m for throughput-heavy model endpoints; matrix documents overrides per route
Autoscale cool-down will be extended to 90s during canary to reduce oscillation; infra agreed to this trade-off after capacity simulations
tasks: ENG: Instrument staging runtime to accept traffic-replay manifests and throttle multipliers (ENG-21344)
SRE: Add GPU utilization and queue-depth metrics to canary dashboards and circuit-breaker hooks
PM: Draft Canary SLA Timing Matrix and circulate for cross-team review
Design: Create a simple Console staging tile to kick off a replay and view results
QA: Define pass/fail gating criteria and automate smoke checks post-replay
risks: Simulating exact production coupling (3rd-party storages or KMS) may be incomplete and produce false positives/negatives
Data residency constraints limit full-trace export to staging for some customers
Overly aggressive automated rollback may cause unnecessary rollbacks during benign transient network events
mitigations: Use 1% trace sampling + synthetic amplification to preserve PII boundaries
Provide a toggle to run replays in a 'safe-mode' that mutes external side-effects (no billing events, no external webhooks)
Matrix includes a human confirmation gate for cases where upstream 3rd-party error rates spike
